Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B
Q2: A
Q3: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Every `placeholder_retired` hold already uses a name ending in `_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`. `scripts/unblock_ledger.py:497` and `unblock_hold_condition` in `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:440` both require that suffix. So option A would turn off every such hold, including the one case that still works. That case is the Q130 path at `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:452-461`: a person sets a repo Actions variable or secret with exactly that name, and the hold ends as `met`. Option B keeps that working path and escalates the steps that can never end that way, such as the action-SHA pin in mongo-explorer#51 and the grant in radateeree-resort.com#174. Option C would need a real variable name taken from free text, which is guesswork the repo cannot back up.
Q2: An operator_step verdict already sends a Telegram WARNING (`scripts/unblock_actions.py:1093`) and already writes the `ai:operator-step` entry under the key `unblock-<item>`. A second alert (option B) would only repeat that. Adding labels (option C) brings in label-repair work this issue does not need. A single comment with a marker, plus the existing resume detection (`unblock_hold_resumed_since`, `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:296-304`), is the smallest change and fully visible to people.
Q3: Both open holds expire under the 14-day default within days: #51 about 2026-11-15 and #174 about 2026-11-18. After that, the judge decides again and takes the new path. Option B would add code that inspects open holds and closes them, for a short-lived benefit and more risk.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/unblock_judge.sh: the verdict comment builder (lines 2383-2395, including the "Stays off behind" line at 2392), `unblock_operator_step_placeholder` (471-487), the fix-up hold writer (1892-1923), `unblock_hold_resume_hint` (307-314), and `unblock_hold_condition` placeholder_retired (439-462)
    - scripts/unblock_ledger.py: `validate`, the operator_step normalisation that keeps `operator_instructions` (1125-1140), the wait / `hold_ref` handling (1117-1124), and the placeholder_retired check (497)
    - scripts/unblock_actions.py: the operator_step ops that use `verdict["operator_instructions"]` (1076-1093)
    - tests/test_unblock_judge.py: the existing placeholder_retired hold tests (about lines 3880-4075, for example `fixup=50 op=hold hold=placeholder_retired ref=DOC_SYNC_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP outcome=held`)
  steps:
    - Decide the step type when the verdict is made, not later. `verdict.json` holds `operator_instructions` only during the verdict run; the item comments read when the fix-up merges do not. A step counts as "set a repo variable or secret" only when `operator_instructions` contain the exact placeholder name and the word "variable" or "secret" (case-insensitive). Anything else counts as some other operator action.
    - Record the result, and the operator instructions as one line, in the trusted verdict comment as new lines next to the existing "Stays off behind `NAME`" line. That comment is already the record the hold writer reads; it is matched by its trusted login and its `ai:unblock:v1` marker.
    - When a fix-up merges, write the `placeholder_retired` hold only if the newest trusted operator_step verdict comment records the variable-or-secret type for that same name. In every other case, take the Q2 escalation path. That includes an older verdict comment that has no type line: treat missing evidence as "escalate", never as "hold".
    - Apply the same rule to model `wait` verdicts with `wait_for.kind == "placeholder_retired"`. Accept them only when the item's newest trusted operator_step verdict comment records the variable-or-secret type for that name. Otherwise `validate` rejects the verdict with a UsageError, so the existing invalid-verdict retry makes the model pick another verdict.
    - Keep `placeholder_retired` in HOLD_KINDS and in the hold-marker regexes (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:285`, the test at `tests/test_unblock_judge.py:5521`) so existing markers still parse, are checked, and expire.
    - Add tests: (1) a fix-up merges for an operator_step whose instructions are not a variable step (for example "pin the action SHA" with `PR_AGENT_ACTION_SHA_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`): no `hold=placeholder_retired` marker is posted and the escalation path runs; (2) a fix-up merges for "set the repository secret NIGHTLY_TOKEN_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP": the current hold behaviour and log line are unchanged; (3) an older verdict comment with no type line escalates; (4) a `wait` verdict on a placeholder that is not a variable step is rejected by `validate`.
    - Add a `changelog.d/` fragment and an `agents.d/<issue>-<slug>.md` fragment for the "Review pipeline consolidator + ledger contract" section. Do not edit agents.md directly. Any new log outcome token gets a "Stable log prefixes (contractual)" entry only if it adds a new prefix.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: The issue's proposed rule, "reject operator-step names matching `*_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`", is narrowed to "reject them unless the verdict's recorded operator instructions say to set a repo variable or secret with exactly that name".
  equivalence_argument: The issue's stated goal is "Do not hold on a variable name nobody will create." Holds on names a person is told to create still end on their own through the Q130 check. All other holds, the ones that cannot end, are refused and escalated. Both reported items fall in the escalated group.
  reversibility: If a person wants option A later, the hold writer can ignore the type line and always escalate. The type line is plain comment text, and the hold kind and marker formats are unchanged.
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/unblock_judge.sh: the fix-up hold writer (1910-1923), `unblock_patch_comment`, and `unblock_hold_resumed_since` (296-304)
    - scripts/unblock_actions.py: the existing `ai:operator-step` entry under key `unblock-<item>` (1079-1092)
  steps:
    - In place of the hold comment, post one comment on the item. It names fix-up #N as done, quotes the recorded operator instructions (for an older verdict comment without them, it points to the open `ai:operator-step` entry `unblock-<item>`), says the judge will not resume the item by itself, and says the person should do the step and then post the item's resume command.
    - End the comment with a new trusted marker in the `ai:unblock-wait:v1` family that is distinct from the hold markers, for example `<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=<n> escalated=operator_step ref=<NAME> -->`. Check that the identifier is not already used. Before posting, look for this marker in the comments already fetched, so the escalation is never posted twice.
    - While the escalation marker is the newest unblock record and no trusted slash command was posted after it (same rule as `unblock_hold_resumed_since`), skip judging the item and log one stable outcome line (for example `outcome=skip reason=operator_escalated`).
    - Close the fix-up wait marker as `done`, the same way the hold path does now. Do not touch the `ai:operator-step` entry. Send no new Telegram alert and add no labels.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: none
  equivalence_argument: This is option A as stated. Each step reuses comment reads and markers that already exist, so the only new API call is the one escalation comment.
  reversibility: Posting the item's resume command clears the escalation, so a person can always take back control.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- none

Assumptions: the hold expiry dates in Q3 come from the question text and the 14-day `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS` default (`scripts/unblock_judge.sh:268-275`); I did not recompute them from the live hold comments. The other consumer repos' code and the real operator instructions for #51 and #174 were not checked; I relied on the issue's statement that nobody will create those names.
